title: Packet Alley
tagline: Keep a city connected. See what each packet does.
menu_intro: The city works because its networks work. Inspect them, make a plan, and watch your changes take effect.
assessment_policy: Before you run: inspect the map, choose evidence, and commit a prediction. Each scored attempt uses one network case. Practice remains available after a mistake.

block.title: Frames on the Block
block.opening: It is opening morning in Packet Alley. The noodle shop, its printers, and the nearby desks share one local network. Before anyone can depend on it, you need to find out what each device knows.
block.example_instruction: A demonstration switch connects two sample computers and a test printer on TEST-NET. Click the first computer to see its IP address; click the printer to see its Ethernet address. Trigger one sample frame. Pause it at the switch, inspect its source MAC, then inspect the switch table after the frame. This demonstration uses distinct addresses and links from all scored missions.

town.title: Routes Across Town
town.opening: The local network is running. Now the shop needs services on the other side of the city. Each router makes its own forwarding decision. Your job is to read those decisions before changing them.
town.example_instruction: A demonstration host on 192.0.2.10/24 sends to 198.51.100.20 through a sample router on 192.0.2.1/24. Click the local prefix, select the router interface, then step through a packet and watch its hop limit decrease. The demonstration is read-only and does not reveal any mission next hops.

wires.title: Handshakes and Delivery
wires.opening: Messages can cross the city. The remaining problem is keeping a conversation open long enough to finish the work. The service desk needs a connection, and the shop needs complete files.
wires.example_instruction: In a demonstration network, a client at 203.0.113.10 and a server at 203.0.113.20 exchange a SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK with numbers different from scored levels. Drag each message into a timeline, inspect the two endpoints, then watch one simulated loss in a separate simplified Go-Back-N teaching example. Label the two protocols separately.

storm.title: When Too Much Arrives
storm.opening: The night market is open. The city is busy, and a small server receives more requests than its link can carry. Your assignment is to observe what fails and explain the evidence.
storm.example_instruction: A sample queue receives two ordinary requests each step while a sample link transmits one. Pause and inspect the queue count, then run to a fixed limit. This is an observation of shared capacity, not an attack or attack-building exercise.

address.debrief: The first order reached the kitchen. The shop can work again.
address.inspect_prompt: Inspect the marked devices and packet headers. Record the evidence you used.
address.predict_prompt: Before running, mark your predicted path or failure point and explain which device record supports it.
address.commit_prompt: Commit this plan and run the network.
address.retry_prompt: The evidence does not yet support this plan. Review the trace, then try a new practice case.
